61E8: Per-level configuration table (20 bytes/row)
Read by $A612: row = $61D4 + 20*(wave-formation-tag+1).
One 20-byte per-level row, confirmed field-by-field from $A612's 6-word SP-trick pop (offsets are byte offsets into the row): $00 word -> $9C57, cursor into the colour-scheme table (see $A54D, values land in $9C59/$9C5A); $02 word -> $9BA5, cursor into this level's timeline table (3 bytes/entry, see enemy_timeline); $04 word -> $9BFD, this level's scenery-script pointer (see scenery_script); $06 word -> combined with the current object's IX+$0A into $9C40/$9C41 (difficulty-scaled fire-rate baseline); $08 word -> low byte to $9C42/$9C43 (fire-timer reload value), high byte to $9C71; $0A word -> low byte to $5B56 and $C2E1 (SRL'd), high byte to $5B7A (screen/timing pokes, exact purpose unconfirmed); $0C-$13 (8 bytes) -> wave-formation-tag threshold table, scanned by $A4E7 (base address kept at $9BA7).

6498: Init menu screen: wipe, draw player boxes, labels, fill buffer
Used by the routines at init_players, show_title_attract, print_high_scores and start_game.
Input
A colour/type for the wipe transition ($9C59)
Sets the wipe colour, runs the $C6A6 wipe effect, draws the player-panel box graphics ($6AD4, which uses $6B09), prints the "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER TWO" label, draws two box variants via $66DE, then fast-fills a buffer at $FA79 downward with the word $3D00 (261 words) using a PUSH-based stack trick, and finally calls $C772.
init_menu_screen 6498 LD ($9C59),A set active colour/type for the wipe effect
649B CALL screen_wipe Screen wipe transition effect
649E CALL draw_panel_borders Draw both players' panel borders
64A1 LD A,$03 "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER TWO"
64A3 CALL print_message Print message N from table $627A
64A6 LD A,$01 select box variant 1
64A8 CALL print_player_score Print a player's score at its HUD position
64AB INC A draw box variant 2
64AC CALL print_player_score
64AF DI disable interrupts, save SP, point SP at fill target $FA79
64B0 LD ($64C8),SP
64B4 LD SP,$FA79
64B7 LD HL,$3D00 HL=fill value $3D00, BC=261 (word count)
64BA LD BC,$0105
init_menu_screen_0 64BD PUSH HL fill loop: push HL twice per iteration (fast memory fill via stack)
64BE PUSH HL
64BF DEC BC
64C0 LD A,C
64C1 OR B
64C2 JR NZ,init_menu_screen_0
64C4 CALL fast_attr_mover Fast column mover
64C7 LD SP,$0000 reset SP (restored by caller)
64CA EI re-enable interrupts, return
64CB RET
64CC: Print character to screen using ROM font (pixel-shifted blit)

65C5: Control code $00: reset $9CC9 row, skip-count 7
C still holds the control code value (0, since dispatch index = code). Zeroes the low byte of $9CC9 (part of the cursor position pair), sets a skip-count of 7 into A, then jumps into $65AB (the tail of the space-handling path) to store that count as the new skip-print flag ($9CCB) and return. Reads like a "reset row / pad N characters" control character; not fully confirmed against live behaviour.

65C8 LD (HL),C
65C9 LD A,$07 skip-count = 7

Simplest handler: just LD ($9CCA),C then return. $9CCA's purpose is not otherwise confirmed.

Used by the routines at draw_panel_borders, 6AF4 and A802.
Input

Fills a 2x2 attribute cell block with colour A, converts that attribute address to the corresponding pixel address, then copies an 8-byte-tall bitmap column from DE into it. Repeats for 4 character columns, alternating between the top and bottom row of the block (BIT 0,C) and stepping to the next attribute row pair every 2 columns (+$22 to L). 7900: Tile block 2x2 table (cell -> 2x2 character block)
Four parallel 256-entry lookup tables ($7900/$7A00/$7B00/$7C00). A background map cell is a single byte, used as the index into all four tables at once; the four bytes read out are the four character codes of a 2x2 tile block: $7900=top-left, $7A00=top-right, $7B00=bottom-left, $7C00=bottom-right. The column decoder $C941 reads one cell, writes the top pair ($7900/$7A00) into buffer row A and the bottom pair ($7B00/$7C00) into row B, so each cell renders as a 2-char-wide by 2-char-tall tile block. See docs/Level-Format.md.

7D00: Initialize IM 2 interrupt vector table and set light ISR
Used by the routine at A5A5.
Standard IM 2 setup: I=$FE (vector table at $FE00), fills $FE00-$FFFF with $FD so every vector reads the byte at $FDFD, which is set to $C3 (JP opcode) - making $FDFD/$FDFE act as a self-modifying "JP (isr-handler)" trampoline used by $A0C4/$A0B0 elsewhere. Points that trampoline at $A0B0 (the light/per-frame ISR) before returning.
init_im2 7D00 DI
7D01 LD A,$FE
7D03 LD I,A
7D05 IM 2
7D07 LD HL,$FE00
7D0A LD A,$FD
init_im2_0 7D0C LD (HL),A
7D0D INC L
7D0E JR NZ,init_im2_0
7D10 INC H
7D11 LD (HL),A
7D12 LD A,$C3
7D14 LD ($FDFD),A
7D17 LD HL,$A0B0 point to per-frame handler $A0B0 (light ISR)
7D1A LD ($FDFE),HL set ISR handler address
7D1D EI
7D1E RET

7D98: Decode 9 graphic blocks, then substitute every other byte via table $9A00
Used by the routine at A5A5.
Called from $A5A5/$A5B2. HL starts at $CA09 and is threaded, unsaved, through all 9 calls to $7DC9/$7DF3 as their shared output cursor - $7DF3 writes decoded graphics data to (HL) and advances it, so HL ends up pointing past everything written by the 9 blocks (overwriting the $CA09 descriptor data in place as it's consumed). The total byte count written (HL-$CA09) is then halved and used as a loop count for a second pass: walking from $CA09, every other byte is treated as an index into a fixed 256-entry table at $9A00 and replaced with the looked-up value in place - a substitution/palette pass over half the decoded stream (the alternating bytes are left untouched).

7D9C LD IX,$F765
7DA0 LD HL,$CA09
7DA3 LD B,$09 9 block-descriptor entries
7DA5 PUSH BC
7DA6 CALL $7DC9 Decode one graphic-block descriptor entry
7DA9 LD DE,$0011
7DAC ADD IY,DE Advance IY to the next 17-byte entry
7DAE POP BC
7DAF DJNZ $7DA5 Loop 9 times
7DB1 LD DE,$CA09
7DB4 AND A
7DB5 SBC HL,DE Total bytes written = HL - $CA09
7DB7 EX DE,HL
7DB8 SRL D Halve the byte count (process every other byte)
7DBA RR E
7DBC LD B,$9A
7DBE INC HL
7DBF LD C,(HL) Substitute this byte via table $9A00
7DC0 LD A,(BC)
7DC1 LD (HL),A
7DC2 INC HL Skip the alternate (untouched) byte
7DC3 DEC DE
7DC4 LD A,D
7DC5 OR E
7DC6 JR NZ,$7DBE Loop until the halved count reaches zero
7DC8 RET
7DC9: Decode one graphic-block descriptor entry (IY-indexed)
Used by the routine at 7D98.
Called 9 times from $7D98's loop, once per 17-byte ($11) IY-indexed entry. Calls $7DF3 to decode the block's data, stores the resulting pointer into IY+$02/$03, then calls $7E4A; if IY+$0E (a repeat count) is nonzero, repeats the $7DF3/$7E4A pair that many more times. Finishes by shifting a flag at IY+$0A and, if IY+$06 is set, incrementing a counter at IY+$0B.

7DCC LD (IY+$02),L

7E4A: Build bit-shifted copies of a graphic block (smooth-scroll variants)
Used by the routine at 7DC9.
Called from $7DC9 after $7DF3 has expanded the block. If IY+$06 is zero, just advances HL past the block (+IY+$0C) and returns. Otherwise: derives a shift-step count from the lowest set bit of IY+$06 doubled, and for each step duplicates the block (LDIR, offset by IY+$0C) into a working copy, then right-shifts every column of it by 1 bit with carry propagating between bytes (RLA/RR (HL)/RRA/ADD HL,DE) - building successive sub-pixel-shifted copies of the graphic for smooth horizontal scrolling.

9A00: Byte bit-reversal (mirror) table: $9A00[i] = reverse of i's 8 bits
256-byte lookup where entry i is i with its bit order reversed (bit 0<->7, 1<->6, ...). Used to horizontally mirror sprite bytes: $7D98 builds each sprite's mirrored half by bit-reversing every other byte through this table, and the masked tile blitters ($B1BE etc.) XOR the bit-reversed pixel byte to draw mirrored sprites.

A000: Object state/animation jump-table (used with $B7F6, various offsets)
One continuous 73-entry word table of code addresses, live-verified: every entry ($A000-$A091) points into valid code ($A445-$C3C7 range). Different routines index into different sub-ranges of this same table via $B7F6 (e.g. $A02A, $A02E, $A038, $A042, $A052, $A076 are all just offsets into it, not separate tables). Ends at $A092, immediately followed by the score-value table at $A094 (see $66B5).

A13A: Dispatch highest-priority pending deferred event
Used by the routines at sfx_next_segment and new_game_reset.
Reads the pending-events bitmask ($9C27) ANDed with an enable/priority mask ($9C28); finds the lowest-numbered surviving bit (highest priority), clears it, and dispatches its handler via the $A042 sub-range of the $A000 jump table. General deferred-event dispatcher (bits set by $66B5 bit 1 HUD-redraw, $A1EA bit 0, $A8CF/$BF57/$C33B/$C373 bit 2, $C8C9 bit 3) - not sound-specific.
dispatch_deferred_event A13A LD HL,$9C28
A13D LD A,($9C27)
A140 AND (HL) Exit if no enabled event pending
A141 RET Z
A142 LD B,(HL) Save current enable mask
A143 PUSH BC
A144 LD B,$FF
A146 LD C,A
A147 LD A,B
dispatch_deferred_event_0 A148 INC B Find lowest set bit (highest priority)
A149 RRA
A14A CP C
A14B JR NC,dispatch_deferred_event_0
A14D AND C Clear the chosen bit from $9C27
A14E LD ($9C27),A
A151 LD A,B B = bit index -> jump-table selector
A152 LD HL,$A042
A155 CALL jump_table_dispatch Jump-table dispatcher
A158 POP AF
A159 LD ($9C28),A Restore the enable mask
A15C SCF
A15D RET

Restricts the event-enable mask $9C28 to bit 7 only, then redraws the active player's HUD panel ($6771). Dispatched by $A13A when the corresponding $9C27 bit is pending.

A162 LD A,$80
A164 AND (HL)
A165 LD (HL),A
A166 LD A,($9C76) get Active player
A169 CALL update_hud_panel Update player's HUD panel

A188 RET
A189: Award bonus life when score threshold reached
Used by the routines at A178 and A802.
Compares a progress value (IX+0) against a threshold table at $9CB8 (indexed by IX+4); if not yet crossed, returns. Otherwise advances the threshold index (IX+4) and, unless lives are already at the cap of 10 (IX+3), grants an extra life and redraws the lives/bombs icon row via $672C.

A18D LD E,(IX+$04)
A190 LD D,$00
A192 LD HL,$9CB8
A195 ADD HL,DE
A196 LD A,(IX+$00)
A199 CP (HL)
A19A RET C
A19B INC (IX+$04)
A19E LD A,(IX+$03)
A1A1 CP $0A
A1A3 RET Z
A1A4 INC A
A1A5 LD (IX+$03),A
A1A8 LD A,($9C76) get Active player

A1AF: Restrict event mask to bit 7, run scenery script
Handler for index $25 of the $A000 jump table (see $B7F6).
Masks the deferred-event enable mask ($9C28) down to just bit 7 (only the highest-priority event class stays enabled), then runs the scenery/event script interpreter ($A3A0). Likely used during a state where only critical events (e.g. game-over) may interrupt while background scenery keeps animating.
A1AF LD HL,$9C28
A1B2 LD A,$80
A1B4 AND (HL)
A1B5 LD (HL),A
A1B6 CALL scenery_script Scenery/event script interpreter
A1B9 RET

A1D4: Request sound effect if higher priority than current
Used by the routines at sfx_req_max and BF42.
Input
A effect priority (high nibble)
Compares the high nibble of A against the currently pending effect's priority (stored at ($A1BA)); if A's priority is >= the current one, updates it, marks ($A1BB)=$80, and sets bit 0 of $9C27 to request dispatch via $A13A/$A222.

A1D5 PUSH BC
A1D6 LD HL,$A1BA
A1D9 LD C,A
A1DA LD A,(HL)
A1DB AND $F0 Mask current pending priority (high nibble)
A1DD LD B,A
A1DE LD A,C
A1DF AND $F0 Mask new request's priority (high nibble)
A1E1 CP B
A1E2 JR C,sfx_request_0 Skip if new priority is lower
A1E4 LD (HL),C Store new priority as pending
A1E5 LD A,$80 Mark ready flag $A1BB=$80
A1E7 LD ($A1BB),A
A1EA LD HL,$9C27 Request dispatch via $9C27 bit 0
A1ED SET 0,(HL)
sfx_request_0 A1EF POP BC
A1F0 POP HL
A1F1 RET
A1F2: Load parameters for the pending sound effect
Used by the routines at A16D and sfx_next_segment.
Reads the pending sound-effect priority (low nibble of $A1BA, set by $A1D4); if zero, jumps to the idle path ($A324). Otherwise indexes an 8-byte-stride parameter table at $A329 by (priority-1), copies 7 bytes into a working buffer at $A1BC, and unpacks further fields from it via nibble/bit extraction. Continues the sound-effect pipeline started by $A1CE/$A1D4/$A13A.
sfx_load_params A1F2 LD A,($A1BA)
A1F5 AND $0F Check priority nibble; jump to idle if zero
A1F7 JP Z,$A324
A1FA DEC A (priority-1)*8 -> byte offset into $A329 table
A1FB RLCA
A1FC RLCA
A1FD RLCA
A1FE LD E,A
A1FF LD D,$00
A201 LD HL,$A329 Point HL at this priority's 8-byte parameter entry
A204 ADD HL,DE
A205 LD DE,$A1BC
A208 LD BC,$0007 Copy first 7 bytes into working buffer $A1BC
A20B LDIR
A20D LD A,(HL) Low nibble of 8th byte -> extra field
A20E AND $0F
A210 LD (DE),A
A211 INC DE
A212 XOR (HL) Combine+rotate for second extra field (high nibble)
A213 RRCA
A214 RRCA
A215 RRCA
A216 RRCA
A217 LD (DE),A
A218 LD HL,$A1C2 C = last copied parameter byte
A21B LD C,(HL)
A21C LD HL,$A1C5 HL -> tone-length source; A = first parameter byte
A21F LD A,($A1BC)
A222: Play sound effect (timed speaker-bit toggle)
Alternates the value written to port $FE between $18 and $00 (toggling bit 4, the speaker/EAR bit, along with border colour bits) inside a precisely NOP-counted delay loop - a square-wave tone generator, same technique as the $AA0F/$AA34 music engine but used here for a sound effect rather than music. Exact trigger context not confirmed.

A231 LD HL,$A1C5
A234 LD E,L
A235 LD D,H
A236 JR Z,sfx_play_tone_0 Pick $A1C5 vs $A1C6 pointer variant

A247 NOP

A3A0: Scenery/event script interpreter (wait or dispatch event)
Used by the routines at A1AF, select_level_colour and new_game_reset.
Reads bytes from a script pointer ($9BFD, defaulting to $6D71 via $A371). If the script-active flag ($9BFF) isn't $FF, returns immediately (see $A3E2 continuation). Otherwise: a byte with the top bit set dispatches a scene event via an offset-chain table at $6E06 (summing B DE-strides to find the target, stored into $9C0C); $FF rewinds the script pointer back to the default ($9BFB) and loops; anything else is a "wait" delay (masked to a nibble, stored at $9BAF) and the script pointer advances. Distinct from the enemy-formation ($AFB8) and object-movement ($B8F9) script systems - likely drives background/scenery timing.

AFB8: Formation script: read next byte, dispatch via $A000 table (SP=addr/RET trick)
Used by the routines at AC8D, AFC3, B005, B072, B0B4, B15B, B1BE, B24A, B2DA, B36A, B3FE, B452, B4AA, B502, B55E, B61A and B72D.
Input
IX formation-script pointer
Reads the byte at (IX), advances IX, then forms address $A0xx (xx = that byte) and jumps there by setting SP to it and executing RET - the byte value doubles as a direct low-byte offset into the same $A000 word table used by $B7F6 elsewhere. Called by 17 different formation/wave routines ($ADB8, $AFC3, $B005, $B072, $B0B4, $B15B, $B1BE, $B24A, $B2DA, $B36A, $B3FE, $B452, $B4AA, $B567, $B5FE, $B61A, $B6BF, $B72D) - this is the shared bytecode-dispatch core of the enemy formation/wave scripting system.
formation_dispatch AFB8 LD L,(IX+$00) read next script byte from (IX), advance script pointer
AFBB INC IX
AFBD LD H,$A0 form address $A0xx from script byte, jump there via faked RET
AFBF LD SP,HL
AFC0 RET
AFC1: Formation opcode $14: jump to (IX)
Handler for index $14 of the $A000 jump table (see $B7F6). A single JP (IX) - an indirect dispatch that continues execution at whatever address IX currently holds.
AFC1 JP (IX)
AFC3: Update tile-block tables ($7900+) from SP-fed data (index $00, INC L)
Handler for index $00 of the $A000 jump table (see $B7F6). Twin of $B072 but fills ascending: writes the low byte of each popped word into a page of the 2x2 tile-block tables ($7900-$7CFF, see $7900), L rising from $F0, then INC H advances to the next page ($7A/$7B/$7C) for each of B ($9C1A) passes. Continues into the formation script ($AFB8).

B072: Update tile-block tables ($7900+) from SP-fed data (index $04)
Handler for index $04 of the $A000 jump table (see $B7F6). Writes into the 2x2 tile-block lookup tables at $7900-$7CFF (see $7900) rather than to the screen. For B ($9C1A) passes it fills a descending run of one page (H=$79, L from $FF down) with the low byte of each popped word, then INC H advances to the next page ($7A/$7B/$7C) - so successive passes populate the parallel quadrant tables. B55E: Copy 8-wide screen strips (SP-trick, screen-third aware)
Handler for index $11 of the $A000 jump table (see $B7F6). Copies vertical 8-byte-wide strips of screen memory using an SP/EX (SP),HL trick to alternate source and destination pointers: each row LDIs 8 bytes then advances by $0024. Column source at $9C0F is range-checked against $C8 to pick which of three copy loops runs ($B577 plain, $B599 with INC H, $B5CE with DEC H) so the copy steps correctly across the ZX screen's non-linear thirds. B730: Initialize wave: build object pool, reset counts, spawn first object
Used by the routine at load_wave_config.
Builds the 19-slot object free-list at $9D40 (linked via IY+0/+1, head at $9D1C), inits 4 fixed slots at $9D1E (stride 6, "active"+"alive" flags set), clears the 15-byte formation-slot bitmap at $9B4F, sets four per-group enemy counts ($9D19=6/$9D18=8/$9D1A=4/$9D1B=1, totalling 19 = pool size), then allocates the first object via $C559. B79F: Mark formation slot done, trigger completion effect when group empties
Used by the routines at BFEB, C015, C075, C11C, C199, C298, C31A, C359, C388 and C3C7.
Input
IY object struct base
Clears/masks a bit in a table at $9B50 (indexed by IY+13, a formation-slot id) then decrements an adjacent per-formation counter; when that counter reaches zero, marks the slot done (IY+13=$FF) and either calls $C648 or $C5D2 (start explosion) depending on the $9C3F flag, then decrements a group counter at $9D18. Entry at $B79F uses C=0 (set bit), entry at $B7A3 uses C=$FF (clear bit) - exact meaning of the $9B50 bitmap not yet confirmed. The tail from $B7DC onward (an SP=IY stack trick) is not yet analyzed.

B7DB RET

B845: Compute angle from object IX to target IY
Used by the routines at BA2B, clamp_player_pos and enemy_fire_steer.
Input
IX object position (shooter)
IY target position (e.g. player)
Rounds IX's fixed-point X/Y position (lo/hi at IX+$0B/$0C and IX+$0D/$0E) to the nearest integer (RLA into the low byte's top bit, then ADC A,$00 on the high byte), subtracts IY's integer column/row (IY+$0C/$0E) to get delta X (C) and delta Y (B), takes their absolute values while recording quadrant bits in D, then refines to an octant and runs a linear-search division ($B889-$B89C) to approximate the angle - a coarse atan2 feeding aiming/movement code such as $C43C.

B84E SUB (IY+$0C) Delta X = rounded IX position minus IY column

B856 LD A,(IX+$0E)
B859 ADC A,$00
B85B SUB (IY+$0E) Delta Y = rounded IX position minus IY row

B869 LD D,$3F

B86C AND A

B876 LD D,A
B877 LD A,C

B8F9: Movement-pattern script interpreter
Used by the routines at C075, C11C, C199 and C217.

Counts down a per-object frame-delay timer (IY+18); once it expires, reads the next byte of a movement script (pointer at IY+15/16) into IY+17, masks it to 0-7, and dispatches that step through the $A076 sub-table (indices $3B-$48) via $B7F6. BE4A: Clamp player position to screen bounds, update bank animation
Clamps the player object's X position ($IY+0B/0C) between $0700 and $18E0, then its Y position (IY+0D/0E) between $0300 and $18E0, then steps a "bank angle" frame (IY+16, target IY+17) toward its target by 1 per call (with a short delay after a direction change) and looks up the resulting sprite frame from a table at $9B4C. none; uses colour from $9C59 (set by caller beforehand)

C941: Decode next column's tile data into ping-pong buffer
Used by the routine at C8B8.
Called from $C8B8 every 8th frame. If the column-ready flag ($9BA2 bit 5) is clear, first calls $C981 to scan/spawn enemies from the previous column. Then decodes 9 map cells from the column-source pointer ($9BA9) into the ping-pong buffer at $9BB0: each cell byte indexes the four 2x2 tile-block tables at $7900-$7CFF (see $7900), and the four resulting character codes are stored as top pair ($7900/$7A00 -> IX+0/IX+1, row A) and bottom pair ($7B00/$7C00 -> IX+$12/IX+$13, row B). So the 9 cells expand to two 18-char column rows. Advances the source pointer ($9BA9) and bumps a level-progress counter ($9BAD) clamped at $1C.

C981: Scan incoming column for spawn markers and allocate enemy objects
Used by the routine at decode_column.
Called from $C941 when the "column ready" flag ($9BA2 bit 5) is clear. Scans 9 entries of the newly-decoded column buffer ($9BA9, stride $10) for spawn markers $05/$55; for each match, calls $BA5F to spawn a group (D = entry offset, used there as the enemy's row/type). $BA5F returns carry set on success: on a successful spawn the marker byte is left unchanged, but if the pool was full (carry clear) the cell is overwritten with $33 to mark it consumed/blocked.

C9AF: Advance enemy timeline: fire due entries and dispatch their commands
Used by the routine at isr_heavy.
Called every frame from $A0C4. Every 16th tick, advances the level-progress counter ($9BA4) and processes all timeline entries whose trigger byte matches it: each 3-byte entry [trigger, param D, command] either dispatches a special command ($FB-$FE) or, for any other value, treats it as a formation tag and spawns via $C9E4/$BA5F. Ends the frame's processing at the first non-matching or $FF entry. See docs/Level-Format.md.
enemy_timeline C9AF LD HL,$9BA3 POKE 51631,201 patches entry to RET, disabling this routine (No Enemies)
C9B2 LD A,(HL)
C9B3 INC A Advance tick counter mod 16; act only every 16th tick
C9B4 AND $0F
C9B6 LD (HL),A
C9B7 RET NZ
C9B8 LD HL,$9BA4
C9BB INC (HL) Advance level-progress counter ($9BA4)
C9BC LD A,(HL)
enemy_timeline_0 C9BD LD HL,($9BA5) Point at current timeline entry ($9BA5)
C9C0 LD A,(HL)
C9C1 CP $FF End of table when trigger byte is $FF
C9C3 JR Z,enemy_timeline_1
C9C5 LD A,($9BA4) get Level progress / index
C9C8 CP (HL) Fire only when progress counter matches the trigger byte
C9C9 JR NZ,enemy_timeline_1
C9CB INC HL Read param D and command byte; advance past 3-byte entry
C9CC LD D,(HL)
C9CD INC HL
C9CE LD A,(HL)
C9CF INC HL
C9D0 LD ($9BA5),HL
C9D3 CP $FC Command $FC: reset $9D1B
C9D5 JR Z,enemy_timeline_4
C9D7 CP $FE Command $FE: set $9C3B=$FF
C9D9 JR Z,enemy_timeline_2
C9DB CP $FD Command $FD: bump counter $9C69
C9DD JR Z,enemy_timeline_3
C9DF CP $FB Command $FB: screen/timing poke ($5B56/$C2E1)
C9E1 JR Z,enemy_timeline_5
C9E3 LD C,A Else: command byte is a formation tag (falls into $C9E4)
C9E4 LD A,$01
C9E6 CALL $BA5F Spawn a group of formation objects from the free-list pool
C9E9 JR enemy_timeline_0
enemy_timeline_1 C9EB RET
enemy_timeline_2 C9EC LD A,$FF
C9EE LD ($9C3B),A
C9F1 RET
enemy_timeline_3 C9F2 LD HL,$9C69
C9F5 INC (HL)
C9F6 JR enemy_timeline_0
enemy_timeline_4 C9F8 XOR A
C9F9 LD ($9D1B),A
C9FC JR enemy_timeline_0
enemy_timeline_5 C9FE LD A,D
C9FF LD ($5B56),A
CA02 SRL A
CA04 LD ($C2E1),A
CA07 JR enemy_timeline_0
CA09: Player-plane masked sprite (24x16, interleaved pixel/mask, mask bit-reversed)
Each frame is 24px wide x 16px tall = 3 vertical 8px strips of 32 bytes (16 rows of a [pixel, mask] pair). The mask byte is stored bit-reversed and must be flipped through the $9A00 table to align with the pixel byte. Successive frames are pre-shifted horizontal copies (each +1px) built by $7E4A for smooth sub-pixel movement; $7DF3 interleaves the pixel/mask pairs and $7D98 generates mirrored halves via $9A00.

FDFD: IM2 interrupt trampoline and vector table
The IM2 vector register I=$FE, so every interrupt reads the word at $FDFD/$FDFE. $FDFD holds a JP opcode ($C3, planted by $7D00), so the CPU executes JP $A0B0 (the ISR). $FE00 onward is the vector table itself, filled with $FD by $7D00 so every table entry points back here to $FDFD; it continues past this block's end ($FE7B) up to $FFFF.
FDFD JP isr_light => Interrupt handler
